themes_detail.label: Park Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints in parks spiked to 4 complaints THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 3100% increase (z-score: 11.72)—suggesting a new or intensifying disturbance pattern in community green spaces during peak-use season.
evidence: 4 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3100% spike, z-score 11.72)
Timing coincides with warming weather and increased park usage
Chronic community board budget request for park improvements suggests longstanding maintenance/amenity gaps
reporting_angles: What specific parks are affected and what is the source of noise (events, vendors, enforcement gaps)?
Interview residents and Parks Dept on enforcement capacity and whether temporary events or construction is driving spike

themes_detail.label: Street/Sidewalk Noise Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 39 THIS WEEK compared to a 10-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 290% increase (z-score: 4.19)—indicating possible new commercial activity, construction, or enforcement failures.
evidence: 39 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 10 weekly baseline (290% increase, z-score 4.19)
Concurrent spike in mobile food vendor complaints 3 weeks ago (2300% above baseline) suggests vendor-related disturbance
Noise-related complaints dominate top-10 311 types across residential and public areas (4248 total complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Are food vendors, construction, or nightlife venues driving the surge? Map 311 complaint locations.
Interview NYPD and SLA on enforcement activity and whether vendor permits or outdoor dining policies have changed

themes_detail.label: Curb Damage & Street Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK versus 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (586% increase, z-score: 5.53), alongside elevated street condition complaints (589 over 90 days), suggesting accelerating street infrastructure failure.
evidence: 6 curb condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (586% spike, z-score 5.53)
589 street condition complaints over 90 days indicates chronic infrastructure gap
Heavy construction activity: 517 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (328 alterations, 122 new buildings) may be exacerbating street damage
reporting_angles: Are DOB-permitted construction projects damaging curbs/streets without adequate restoration? Cross-reference complaint locations with active DOB permits.
Interview DOB and Department of Transportation on curb repair backlogs and whether construction oversight is sufficient

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 39 three weeks ago versus a 4.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (818% increase, z-score: 8.57), though timing is slightly older; if sustained or worsening this week, indicates organized vandalism or enforcement breakdown.
evidence: 39 graffiti complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 4.2 weekly baseline (818% spike, z-score 8.57)
Timing predates this week but magnitude suggests organized activity or systemic enforcement gap
Convergence with elevated noise and vendor complaints indicates broader public order concerns
reporting_angles: Interview Sanitation Dept on graffiti removal capacity and whether crews are keeping pace with new tagging
Investigate whether specific corridors or property types are being targeted; identify any community or gang-related patterns

themes_detail.label: Tree Health Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints surged to 3 last week versus 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% increase, z-score: 5.42), suggesting environmental stress or deferred maintenance as warming season accelerates visible decline.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Chronic community board budget request for park/amenity improvements reflects underinvestment in green infrastructure
Spring season may be exposing winter damage or revealing trees stressed by poor maintenance
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Dept on tree inventory health and whether pest or disease outbreak is occurring
Investigate whether specific neighborhoods lack adequate tree care; connect to equity and heat resilience concerns
